tromost: Prešeren Square and the Triple Bridge

The heart of Ljubljana: the square with the monument to the poet France Prešeren, the pink Franciscan church and the three side-by-side bridges over the Ljubljanica river, designed by the architect Jože Plečnik. The whole old town starts here.
vecchio: Old Town: Stari trg, Mestni trg and Dragon Bridge
The streets of medieval Ljubljana below the castle hill, with colourful houses, shops and bars along the river. To the north, the 1901 Dragon Bridge has four bronze dragons, the city's symbol.
mercato: Central Market, Plečnik's Colonnade and Cathedral

The open-air market on Vodnik Square and the stalls under Plečnik's long riverside colonnade: fruit, vegetables, cheese, cured meats, honey and local produce. Next to it is the Baroque St Nicholas' Cathedral, with its bronze doors.
castello: The medieval castle overlooking the city from its hill, with a lookout tower from which you see all of Ljubljana as far as the Alps, the museum of Slovenian history and the "virtual castle" show. Go up in 3 minutes by funicular or on foot in about 15–20 minutes.
crociera: A 50-minute boat trip along the river, under the bridges of the centre, with a guide telling the city's history. An easy way to see Ljubljana from a different angle and rest your legs.
tivoli: The city's great park, a few minutes from the centre, with tree-lined avenues, Cekin Mansion and Tivoli Castle in the background. It's where Ljubljana's residents go running and walking.
congressi: Congress Square and the National Library

The great 1821 square where the European powers met after Napoleon, with the University, the Philharmonic and the park. A few steps away is Plečnik's National and University Library, with its stone-and-brick façade.
